subject: Film & Cinema
title: The French New Wave Explosion
description: A micro-lesson that makes The French New Wave Explosion usable.

hook.text: In 1959, a 27-year-old film critic released his first feature. It changed everything.

buildup.text: François Truffaut's The 400 Blows launched the French New Wave alongside Godard and Varda.

discovery.text: They shot on streets, used jump cuts, broke the fourth wall, and ignored studio rules.

twist.text: The movement's directors eventually split — Godard went radical, Truffaut went classical.

climax.text: The New Wave made personal cinema respectable and inspired movements on every continent.

punchline.text: Critics picked up cameras and rewrote cinema.
